## Executive summary

Sprint 44 was a blocked sprint. The upstream identity provider rolled out a breaking change on the v3 endpoints on day five, idling three engineers for nine days while the team built and tested a compatibility shim. Velocity landed at **41 story points** versus a 63 SP baseline, a **35 percent miss**. Salvaged value across the usage heatmap drill down, daily digest close out, and the permission matrix audit log search UI shipping to GA.

## Highlights

- **Identity provider compatibility shim delivered on day eleven.** Spiked, built, and validated against staging. The auth migration cutover is now rescheduled for Sprint 45 day twelve.
- **Usage heatmap drill down** (per user activity timeline) shipped. Customer Success picked it up in the Sprint 44 review session and asked for one more cut by industry, captured as a Sprint 46 follow up.
- **Daily digest email closed end to end** across backend wiring, the A B test setup, and the open rate dashboard wiring. Open rate dashboard moved from in review to done on day twelve.
- **Permission matrix audit log search UI shipped,** paired with a clean RBAC documentation refresh.

## Watch list

- **Five tickets blocked at the close.** Auth migration production cutover plan (8 SP), smoke test suite (5 SP), SSO tenant provisioning script update (3 SP), customer comms draft (2 SP), and the rollback runbook (3 SP in review). All five carry over to Sprint 45.
- **Auth team morale.** Three engineers idled for nine days, two of them seniors who had the context. Worth a one on one with Alex Chen and Priya Sharma to acknowledge the cost and reset expectations.
- The retrospective notes ticket sits in to do. If we want this lesson captured, the engineering manager needs to pick it up by Sprint 45 day three.

## Recommendations

- Open a conversation with the identity provider on a 30 day advance notice policy for breaking changes on v3 endpoints. Our entire auth migration was blocked because the deprecation surfaced mid sprint with zero prior signal.
- Build the fallback compatibility shim into the migration runbook before the Sprint 45 retry. The shim that landed this sprint is now repo level infrastructure, but the runbook needs to call it out so the next migration cannot get blocked the same way.
- Park the daily digest open rate analysis until Sprint 47. The dashboard is live, but pulling insight from one week of data is premature.

## Talking points

- **Blocked sprint** driven by an unannounced breaking change from the upstream identity provider.
- **Velocity 41 SP versus 63 SP baseline.** A 35 percent miss, fully attributable to the blocker.
- **Compatibility shim delivered on day eleven.** Auth migration cutover rescheduled for Sprint 45.
- **Salvaged value of 41 SP** across heatmap drill down, daily digest, and permission matrix work. The team did not stall.
- **Five tickets carry into Sprint 45,** all on the auth migration critical path.
